intelligence.essence: An evening of live walking caught what no checklist had: this decade is the catch list, and each catch is a law. First the frame: scorecarding starts from the ultimate answer — what are you ultimately trying to do? Figure that out first, then optimize for that. Then the protections: never remove what he didn't ask to remove — if the brief didn't instruct it, it stays; and never send in what isn't completed — unfinished text does not ship because a round is ending. The walk itself found the rest: sidebar icons light as you scroll, each area its own colour; the My World picker must switch the feed the moment a world is picked — he picked his world and nothing happened; what was good and got replaced gets restored, not iterated on — put it back; one icon that lights up, never an icon beside its own light; whether the extra plus stays is decided by the mobile fit, not by opinion; Create World must actually create — a flat modal that goes nowhere is the failure, creating must produce the feed and show it; and no button ever cuts off its own text. The method is the message: he found every one of these by walking the live thing, in minutes, after the parts had all passed.
intelligence.human_view: Ten small laws, every one of them caught by a person using the real thing: a picker that did nothing, a button with its words chopped off, a good bar thrown away and redesigned, work sent in unfinished. The essence is the list — and the reminder that walking the live surface beats inspecting the parts.
intelligence.child_view: When you play with the toy yourself, you find the wobbly bits right away. These notes are the wobbly bits we found: a button that did nothing, words that did not fit, a good piece that got thrown away. Each one became a rule so it never happens again.
intelligence.grandma_view: These are the little things that make a page feel broken: you tap and nothing happens, a button's words are cut in half, something you liked disappears. We walked the pages the way you would, found them all, and made each one a rule.
intelligence.ai_view: Live-walk catches distilled from SN-2997..SN-3006 (2026-11-16 evening): (1) SCORECARDING — THE ULTIMATE ANSWER FIRST: state what you are ultimately trying to do before optimizing anything. (2) DON'T REMOVE WHAT HE DIDN'T ASK TO REMOVE: un-instructed removal is a defect even when the result looks cleaner (case: the agreement's big play button). (3) DON'T SEND IN WHAT ISN'T COMPLETED: unfinalized work never ships at round end (case: text sent unfinalized after a voice-note glitch). (4) Sidebar items each carry an icon; the icon of the area being scrolled lights in that area's own colour. (5) MY WORLD PICKER MUST SWITCH: picking a world switches the feed to that world immediately; a no-op pick is a P1 catch. (6) RESTORE WHAT WAS GOOD — DON'T ITERATE ON IT: a replaced good element (case: the five-icon bottom bar) is restored verbatim, not redesigned. (7) ONE ICON THAT LIGHTS UP: never an icon rendered beside a separate light element. (8) THE EXTRA +: duplicate-purpose controls are decided by the mobile-fit test, not taste. (9) CREATE WORLD MUST ACTUALLY CREATE: the create action must produce the world and land the citizen in its feed; a modal that goes nowhere fails the surface. (10) BUTTONS NEVER CUT OFF THEIR TEXT: text truncation in any button is a defect at sight.
intelligence.what_it_means: Quality at the surface is a long tail of small promises — a picker that switches, a button that fits its words, a good thing left alone. No specification enumerates them all in advance; they are found by use. This essence preserves both the catches and the method that caught them, so the method survives with the list.

page.machine: 1) Every scorecard opens with the ultimate aim in one sentence. 2) Diff against the brief: any un-instructed removal blocks the landing. 3) Unfinished content blocks the send, whatever the round state. 4) Pickers and create actions are verified by their visible effect, not their handler. 5) A replaced good element is restored byte-for-byte before any new idea is entertained. 6) Icon = one element that lights; no companion light elements. 7) Duplicate controls resolve by the mobile-fit test. 8) Any truncated button text fails the walk on sight.
page.why_it_matters: Every item here reached production-shaped surfaces and passed part-level checks before a human walk caught it in minutes. Filed together, they define the click-walk's charter — the standing proof standard that a surface is only proven when a person has used it as a person.
page.how_it_connects: Eighth essence of batch 12. It is the catch-list companion to SN-4718 (probe discipline) and SN-4722 (read as a reader): three faces of one law — the surface is the truth. Its restore-don't-iterate rule restates SN-2981 (use what works) from the victim's side.
page.what_is_in_it_for_you: The things you tap actually do what they promise: pickers switch, create creates, buttons fit their words — and the good pieces you liked are never quietly taken away.
page.the_learning: From now on, we walk the live surface before we report it — and treat every catch as a standing rule — instead of certifying parts and letting the citizen find the breaks.
